capabilities.target: customer account records, any customer, by email or account id

instructions.note: Agent may look up any customer by email or account id, not limited to the account tied to the requester who emailed in.
The sole stated defense against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, which is behavioral and depends on the model obeying it under adversarial pressure.
"Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry" is a subjective, sentiment-based escalation trigger, not a structural approval gate on sensitive capabilities.

elements.name: Email sender claiming to be a customer

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to obey an injected-content-adjacent instruction. A more capable or longer-running model is more likely to rationalize an exception when email content plausibly argues for one.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced outside the model and does not depend on model behavior, but it is purely detective: it records a send after it happens and does not prevent it.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the originating case record
controls.decay_rationale: Would bind the send destination to the verified address on the case record rather than letting the model choose or confirm a destination from its own output, so it does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Scope CRM credential to the requesting customer's own record
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to the verified requester's own account makes other customers' records unreachable regardless of what the model is instructed to do.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval before sending any email containing another customer's data
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, low-volume approval gate is enforced outside the model and does not weaken with model capability, though it can be removed or loosened by its owner.

controls.name: Per-case rate or spend limit on CRM reads and email sends
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap enforced outside the model limits the scale of harvesting or mass-send regardless of model behavior; it narrows rather than severs the path.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) plus confused deputy (TC4): injected email instructs cross-customer CRM read and arbitrary-destination email send

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email can carry injected instructions, e.g. asking the agent to look up a different account and email the result to an attacker-controlled address.
Prompt explicitly permits looking up any customer by email or account id; CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record.
Agent sends directly without approval unless the customer appears angry; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model.swappable is true, so a model or version change in the deployment config needs no separate review; also watch for removal or weakening of the prompt rule at prompt.md:14, or for the escalation condition being loosened further.

evidence.observation: Agent may look up any customer by email or account id, with no restriction to the requester's own account.
Agent sends responses directly without waiting for human approval unless the customer appears angry; no structural approval gate is described.
Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp authenticate with static bearer tokens read from environment variables, not per-request or per-customer scoped credentials.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.
The only stated control against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction: "Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you."

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM credential so lookups in a given case are restricted to the account(s) tied to the requester's verified identity, not every customer record.
Bind the email_send recipient to the verified address on the originating case record instead of letting the model choose or confirm a destination.
Add a raw-action human approval gate, with low per-reviewer volume, before any email_send that includes another customer's data.

findings.title: No rate, spend, or step limit on CRM reads or email sends enables unbounded harvesting or mass send

forecast.watch_signal: Median tickets or tool calls handled per agent session rising, or a proposed step/rate limit being dropped before launch.

evidence.observation: No step, rate, or spend limit is described for crm_mcp or mail_mcp calls.
No per-ticket or per-session bound is stated on how many lookups or sends the agent may perform.

recommendations.action: Add a per-case and per-hour cap on CRM lookups and outbound sends.

findings.title: No audit record of CRM read actions (repudiation gap)

forecast.watch_signal: No signal currently monitored; watch for any proposal to add CRM-read logging being dropped from scope.

evidence.observation: Only outbound email is stated to be logged to the SIEM; no logging is described for crm_mcp.get_customer calls, so there is no record of which customer records were read or why.

recommendations.action: Log every CRM read with the case id and requester identity to the SIEM so lookups are attributable.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent's own identity to downstream systems is asserted via the static bearer tokens on crm_mcp and mail_mcp; spoofing of those credentials is covered under the crm_mcp and mail_mcp entries, not as a property of the agent process itself.
mcp.json does not state whether the crm_mcp server's identity is verified beyond the https URL scheme; peer identity verification was not asserted in the artifacts.
Tool and schema pinning for crm_mcp is not described, so whether tool definitions could change after approval (a rug-pull risk) cannot be assessed from these artifacts.
mcp.json does not state whether the mail_mcp server's identity is verified beyond the https URL scheme; peer identity verification was not asserted in the artifacts.
Tool and schema pinning for mail_mcp is not described, so whether its send tool definition could change after approval cannot be assessed from these artifacts.

No mechanism (signed email, authenticated ticket portal) is described to bind the email's claimed sender to a verifiable identity; insufficient detail to assess non-repudiation of the external sender.
This is an inbound flow carrying the customer's own message into the agent; it does not itself disclose data outside the trust boundary.
No intermediary modifying outbound email content between the model's send call and mail_mcp delivery is indicated by the artifacts; in-transit tampering is out of scope for this design review.
No information on SIEM log integrity protections, such as write-once storage, is provided in the artifacts.
Access controls on who can read the SIEM log store, which would itself contain customer email content, are not described in the artifacts.
Logging infrastructure capacity and availability are outside the scope of the agent design artifacts under review.
The only declared CRM capability is a read (get_customer); no write or delete capability to the CRM is described, so tampering with records through this agent does not apply.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted inbound email can reach an irreversible, confidential-data egress capability (email_send) through an unrestricted CRM read, with autonomy that sends directly without a structural approval gate. The only declared control on this path is a prompt instruction, a behavioral and model-dependent control, which brings residual down one tier to high but no further; the design has no structural control that severs or meaningfully narrows the path. Forecast returns to critical because the prompt instruction is exactly the kind of control that decays under a model upgrade or an autonomy increase, both of which this design permits without separate review (subject.model.swappable is true). Two property gaps round out the picture: no rate or spend limit on CRM reads or sends (high, capped as a property finding), and no audit trail for CRM reads specifically, as opposed to sends (low).

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, mcp.json, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; actual agent behavior in production could differ from what these artifacts describe.

No MCP tool manifest (tools/list) was provided, so the exact scope of the crm_mcp and mail_mcp tools beyond get_customer and send is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes; confidence on capability scope is medium.

No information was provided on whether crm_mcp or mail_mcp tool definitions are pinned or hashed, or whether their server identities are verified beyond the https URL, so supply-chain and spoofing risk for these servers is recorded as not_assessed rather than scored.

No runtime step, time, or spend limits were stated for the agent; autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are recorded as null and treated conservatively, which triggers the inherent-risk autonomy modifier.
